newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OVERTIME GOAL LIFTS SABRES PAST BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OVERTIME GOAL LIFTS SABRES PAST BRUINS.

text.p: Michal Grosek, in a crowd at the net, put a backhander past Scott Bailey at 2:39 of overtime to give the Buffalo Sabres a 3-2 win over the Boston Bruins Saturday.
Matthew Barnaby tried a wraparound at the left goal post, but ended up centering the puck off Derek Plante's skate and into the crease, where Grosek lifted a backhander over Bailey's glove.

"I think they got a little nervous seeing so many guys scramble in front of the net," said Barnaby. "They all tried to cover a man but they left me open. I just tried to get it on net and Grosek was there with the empty-netter."
"It's one thing we really wanted to start doing, not just this game but the last five or six games," Buffalo coach Ted Nolan said."We have to drive the net and go in for some rebounds.
"Earlier in the year we were trying for those pretty goals. When you go to the net, lucky things happen once in a while."
The triumph ended Buffalo's six-game winless streak at Boston, where the Sabres had not won since October 1993.
Randy Burridge and Brian Holzinger had the other Buffalo goals. Ray Bourque had a goal and an assist for the Bruins.
In St Louis, Ray Sheppard set up the tying goal in the second period and scored the game-winner less than two minutes later as the Florida Panthers defeated the Blues for the first time, 3-1.
Mark Fitzpatrick stopped 29 shots for Florida, which was 0-3-1 in four previous meetings with St Louis. The Panthers improved the league's best road record to 7-1-3.
Florida, which improved to 4-1-1 in its last six games, has the league's best record at 14-3-1.

At Los Angeles, linemates Brendan Shanahan and Steve Yzerman continued their torrid scoring with two goals and two assists apiece and Chris Osgood stopped 26 shots for his 11th career shutout as the Detroit Red Wings routed the Kings 6-0.

Shanahan has four goals and six assists in his last four games. Yzerman has been even hotter with five goals and 10 assists in his last six contests. Yzerman, tied with Gordie Howe for the Red Wing lead in career hat tricks, missed a pair of chances at his third goal of the game in the final period.
In Ottawa, red-hot Bruce Gardiner scored off a rebound with 2:07 left in regulation and the Senators rallied from a three-goal deficit to tie the Hartford Whalers, 3-3.
Gardiner got his fourth goal in three games after failing to score in his first 14 games.
Daniel Alfredsson had the other two goals for the Senators, who have beaten Hartford only once in 12 meetings at home (1-8-3).
Geoff Sanderson tallied twice for the first-place Whalers.
In Vancouver, ex-Ranger Mike Ridley scored twice, including the go-ahead goal late in the second period, and the Canucks rallied for a 5-3 victory over freefalling New York.
Alexander Mogilny added a goal and an assist for Vancouver, which has won three straight and swept a season series with the Rangers for the first time.
The Rangers, who have lost three straight, are 1-7-1 in their last nine games and fell six games below .500.
In San Jose, Paul Kariya scored twice, Teemu Selanne had a pair of assists and Guy Hebert made 25 saves for his first shutout of the season as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim blanked the Sharks, 3-0.
Anaheim won for the second time in six games (2-3-1). The Sharks are winless in their last six games (0-5-1).
In Phoenix, Keith Tkachuk scored with 17 seconds left in the third period to cap a three-goal comeback as the Coyotes tied the New York Islanders 3-3 in a matchup of floundering last-place teams.
The Coyotes have one win in their last nine games (1-5-3). The Islanders are winless in their last five games (0-2-3).

At Tampa Bay, Dale Hawerchuk redirected Eric Desjardins' slap shot past goaltender Corey Schwab with just under five minutes remaining in regulation to lift the Philadelphia Flyers past the Lightning 2-1.
The Flyers have won five straight road games and could get superstar centre Eric Lindros back within the week.
In Toronto, Marc Bureau's goal with 7:23 remaining in regulation snapped a tie and lifted the Montreal Canadiens to a 4-3 defeat of the Maple Leafs.

Montreal goaltender Jocelyn Thibault made the lead stand by stonewalling Doug Gilmour on an odd-man rush with just under five minutes left. Gilmour bowled over Thibault attempting to push home a loose puck and the red light went on. But replay officials ruled no goal, preserving the lead.
In Edmonton, Mariusz Czerkawski's goal at 1:38 snapped a third-period tie and Andrei Kovalenko scored twice as the Oilers edged the sputtering Calgary Flames 3-2.
The Flames dropped their third straight and 2-8-1 in their last 11 games.
At Washington, Peter Bondra's breakaway goal with 3:34 remaining gave the Capitals a 4-3 victory over the New Jersey Devils and a sweep of their home-and-home series.
